questions.stem: A 64-year-old man is treated with PCI for an anterior STEMI. He recovers well. On day 5 he has new pressure-like chest pain that lasts 40 minutes. The pain does not change with breathing or position, and there is no friction rub. The ECG shows new ST depression in leads V4-V6. His lab results are: day 1, troponin I 38 ng/mL and CK-MB 92 ng/mL; day 3, troponin I 21 ng/mL and CK-MB 4 ng/mL; day 5, troponin I 26 ng/mL and CK-MB 41 ng/mL (reference: troponin I < 0.04 ng/mL, CK-MB < 5 ng/mL). Which is the most likely cause of the new chest pain?
choices: Early fibrinous pericarditis
Reinfarction
Dressler syndrome
Rupture of the left ventricular free wall
Coronary vasospasm without necrosis
questions.explanation: **CK-MB** returns to normal about **2-3 days** after an MI, so its **new rise** on day 5, together with new ischemic pain and ECG changes, shows **reinfarction**. Troponin stays high for **7-10 days** after the first MI, so it alone cannot separate the old injury from a new one. Early pericarditis is the tempting choice in the first days, but its pain is pleuritic and positional, often with a rub, and it does not cause a new CK-MB peak. Vasospasm without necrosis would not raise CK-MB again.
questions.explanation_pt: A **CK-MB** volta ao normal cerca de **2-3 dias** após o IAM, então sua **nova elevação** no 5º dia, junto com nova dor isquêmica e alterações no ECG, indica **reinfarto**. A troponina permanece elevada por **7-10 dias** após o primeiro IAM, então ela sozinha não separa a lesão antiga de uma nova. A pericardite precoce é a alternativa tentadora nos primeiros dias, mas sua dor é pleurítica e posicional, muitas vezes com atrito, e ela não causa novo pico de CK-MB. Um vasoespasmo sem necrose não elevaria a CK-MB novamente.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman had an anterior STEMI 5 weeks ago and was treated with PCI. Now she has 3 days of fever and sharp chest pain. The pain is worse when she breathes in and better when she sits up and leans forward. Temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). A pericardial friction rub is heard. Lab results: leukocytes 11,200/mm3, ESR 64 mm/h, troponin I normal, serum creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. Which mechanism best explains her condition?
choices: Fibrinous inflammation spreading from a recent transmural infarct
Bacterial infection introduced during cardiac catheterization
Bleeding into the pericardium from a ruptured ventricular wall
Immune response against heart antigens released by the infarct
Uremic toxins acting on the pericardial surface
questions.explanation: Fever, pleuritic and positional chest pain and a friction rub **weeks** after an MI suggest **Dressler syndrome**, an **autoimmune** pericarditis against myocardial antigens exposed by necrosis. Fibrinous pericarditis that spreads directly from a transmural infarct is the tempting choice, but it appears in the first **1-3 days**, not 5 weeks later. Normal troponin argues against a new infarct, normal creatinine excludes uremic pericarditis, and free-wall rupture causes sudden tamponade, not fever.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre, dor torácica pleurítica e posicional e atrito pericárdico **semanas** após um IAM sugerem **síndrome de Dressler**, uma pericardite **autoimune** contra antígenos miocárdicos expostos pela necrose. A pericardite fibrinosa que se estende diretamente de um infarto transmural é a alternativa tentadora, mas surge nos primeiros **1-3 dias**, não 5 semanas depois. A troponina normal fala contra um novo infarto, a creatinina normal exclui pericardite urêmica, e a ruptura de parede livre causa tamponamento súbito, não febre.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man had a large anterior MI 7 weeks ago. He arrived late and did not receive reperfusion. Now he has mild shortness of breath on exertion. The ECG shows Q waves in leads V1-V4 with ST elevation that has not resolved since the infarct. Troponin is normal. Echocardiography shows a thin apical segment of the left ventricle with a wide neck; this segment moves outward during systole. For which complication of this lesion is he at greatest risk?
choices: Rupture of the bulging wall with cardiac tamponade
Acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture
Systemic embolism from a mural thrombus
Left-to-right shunt across the ventricular septum
Constrictive pericarditis with diastolic heart failure
questions.explanation: Persistent ST elevation weeks after an anterior MI and a thin, **dyskinetic** wide-necked bulge describe a **true ventricular aneurysm**. Blood **stasis** in the aneurysm favors a **mural thrombus**, which can embolize to the brain or other organs. Rupture is the tempting choice, but a true aneurysm has a wall of dense **scar** and rarely ruptures; a high risk of rupture belongs to a **pseudoaneurysm** (contained free-wall rupture with a narrow neck). Papillary muscle and septal ruptures happen about **3-14 days** after an MI, through soft necrotic tissue.
questions.explanation_pt: Supradesnivelamento persistente do ST semanas após um IAM anterior e um abaulamento fino, **discinético** e de colo largo descrevem um **aneurisma ventricular verdadeiro**. A **estase** sanguínea no aneurisma favorece um **trombo mural**, que pode embolizar para o cérebro ou outros órgãos. A ruptura é a alternativa tentadora, mas o aneurisma verdadeiro tem parede de **cicatriz** densa e raramente se rompe; o alto risco de ruptura é do **pseudoaneurisma** (ruptura contida da parede livre, com colo estreito). As rupturas de músculo papilar e do septo ocorrem cerca de **3-14 dias** após o IAM, através do tecido necrótico amolecido.

questions.stem: A 73-year-old man is in the hospital 4 days after an anterior STEMI. He did not receive reperfusion. He suddenly becomes short of breath and hypotensive. A new loud holosystolic murmur is heard. A pulmonary artery catheter is placed, and oxygen saturation is measured: superior vena cava 68%, right atrium 69%, right ventricle 85%, pulmonary artery 86%, systemic artery 94%. Which structure has most likely ruptured?
choices: Posteromedial papillary muscle
Anterolateral papillary muscle
Left ventricular free wall
Chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
Interventricular septum
questions.explanation: The oxygen saturation **steps up** from 69% in the right atrium to 85% in the right ventricle, so oxygenated blood enters the right ventricle from the left: a **left-to-right shunt** through a **ruptured interventricular septum**. The anterior septum is supplied by the **LAD**, which fits an anterior MI. Papillary muscle rupture is the tempting choice because it also gives a new holosystolic murmur and pulmonary edema, but acute mitral regurgitation does not raise right-sided oxygen saturation. Free-wall rupture causes tamponade without a new murmur.
questions.explanation_pt: Há um **salto oximétrico** de 69% no átrio direito para 85% no ventrículo direito, então sangue oxigenado entra no ventrículo direito a partir do esquerdo: um **shunt esquerda-direita** por **ruptura do septo interventricular**. O septo anterior é irrigado pela **DA** (artéria descendente anterior), o que combina com um IAM anterior. A ruptura de músculo papilar é a alternativa tentadora porque também causa novo sopro holossistólico e edema pulmonar, mas a insuficiência mitral aguda não eleva a saturação de oxigênio nas câmaras direitas. A ruptura de parede livre causa tamponamento sem novo sopro.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with hypertension and a long history of smoking dies of a myocardial infarction. At autopsy, the left anterior descending artery has a large plaque. Under the microscope, the plaque has a core of lipid, cholesterol clefts and cell debris. A fibrous cap of smooth muscle cells and collagen covers the core. The smooth muscle cells in the cap came from the media of the artery. Which mediator most directly caused these cells to move into the intima and divide?
choices: Platelet-derived growth factor
Vascular endothelial growth factor
Interleukin-8
Thromboxane A2
Leukotriene B4
questions.explanation: In atherosclerosis, activated endothelial cells, platelets and macrophages release **PDGF**, which makes **smooth muscle cells** migrate from the media into the intima and proliferate. These cells make the collagen of the **fibrous cap**. Interleukin-8 and leukotriene B4 are tempting because they are chemotactic, but they mainly attract **neutrophils**. VEGF drives new vessel growth, and thromboxane A2 causes platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction.
questions.explanation_pt: Na aterosclerose, células endoteliais ativadas, plaquetas e macrófagos liberam **PDGF**, que faz as **células musculares lisas** migrarem da camada média para a íntima e proliferarem. Essas células produzem o colágeno da **capa fibrosa**. A interleucina-8 e o leucotrieno B4 são tentadores porque são quimiotáticos, mas atraem principalmente **neutrófilos**. O VEGF estimula a formação de novos vasos, e o tromboxano A2 causa agregação plaquetária e vasoconstrição.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy dies in a car crash. At autopsy, the inner surface of the aorta has several flat, yellow streaks. They do not raise the surface and do not narrow the lumen. No other vascular lesions are found. Which of the following most likely makes up most of these streaks?
choices: Smooth muscle cells surrounded by dense collagen
Neutrophils within a fibrin-rich exudate
Cholesterol crystals in an extracellular necrotic core
Macrophages filled with lipid droplets
Calcium deposits within the media of the artery
questions.explanation: Flat yellow streaks in a young person are **fatty streaks**, the earliest lesion of atherosclerosis. They are made mainly of **foam cells**: **macrophages** that took up oxidized LDL in the intima. Smooth muscle cells with collagen are the tempting choice, but they form the **fibrous cap** of a later, raised plaque. A necrotic core with cholesterol crystals also belongs to an established plaque, and calcium in the media describes **Mönckeberg** sclerosis.
questions.explanation_pt: Estrias amarelas planas em um jovem são **estrias gordurosas**, a lesão mais precoce da aterosclerose. Elas são formadas principalmente por **células espumosas**: **macrófagos** que captaram LDL oxidada na íntima. Células musculares lisas com colágeno são a alternativa tentadora, mas formam a **capa fibrosa** de uma placa elevada, mais tardia. Um núcleo necrótico com cristais de colesterol também pertence a uma placa estabelecida, e cálcio na camada média descreve a esclerose de **Mönckeberg**.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man has an inferior STEMI. PCI restores flow in the right coronary artery 4 hours after the pain started. Twenty hours later he develops ventricular fibrillation and cannot be resuscitated. At autopsy, many myocytes in the infarct contain dense, irregular, eosinophilic bands that run across the fibers. Which process most directly produced these bands?
choices: Infiltration by neutrophils that release proteases
Calcium influx into myocytes as flow returns
Fatty change from impaired fatty acid oxidation
Collagen deposition by activated fibroblasts
Dystrophic calcification of necrotic myocytes
questions.explanation: **Contraction band necrosis** is typical of **reperfusion**. When blood returns to injured myocytes, their damaged membranes let in a large amount of **calcium**, and the sarcomeres contract too strongly and stay contracted, forming dense transverse bands. Dystrophic calcification is the tempting choice because it also involves calcium, but it is a later deposit of calcium salts in dead tissue, seen as basophilic material, not as contracted sarcomeres. Neutrophils are a cellular infiltrate, and collagen appears weeks later.
questions.explanation_pt: A **necrose em bandas de contração** é típica da **reperfusão**. Quando o sangue volta aos miócitos lesados, suas membranas danificadas permitem a entrada de grande quantidade de **cálcio**, e os sarcômeros se contraem com força excessiva e permanecem contraídos, formando bandas transversais densas. A calcificação distrófica é a alternativa tentadora porque também envolve cálcio, mas é um depósito tardio de sais de cálcio em tecido morto, visto como material basofílico, não como sarcômeros contraídos. Os neutrófilos são um infiltrado celular, e o colágeno surge semanas depois.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension is in the hospital 5 days after her first MI, a lateral STEMI that was not reperfused. She suddenly has chest pain and becomes confused. Pulse is 124/min. Systolic blood pressure is 92 mm Hg during expiration and 74 mm Hg during inspiration. Jugular veins are distended, the lungs are clear, and the heart sounds are muffled. No new murmur is heard. Which finding is most likely on bedside echocardiography?
choices: Effusion with diastolic collapse of the right ventricle
Flail mitral leaflet with a large regurgitant jet into the atrium
Color flow jet across the interventricular septum
Dilated, hypokinetic right ventricle with no effusion
Thin, dyskinetic apical bulge of scar with a wide neck
questions.explanation: Hypotension, distended jugular veins, muffled heart sounds and an **18 mm Hg** inspiratory fall in systolic pressure (**pulsus paradoxus**) 5 days after an MI suggest **free-wall rupture** with **cardiac tamponade**. Echocardiography shows pericardial fluid that compresses the right heart, with **diastolic collapse of the right ventricle**. Right ventricular infarction is the tempting choice because it also gives hypotension, distended neck veins and clear lungs, but it occurs with **inferior** MI in the first hours to days and does not cause muffled heart sounds or marked pulsus paradoxus. A flail mitral leaflet and a septal jet would each produce a new murmur.
questions.explanation_pt: Hipotensão, estase jugular, bulhas abafadas e queda inspiratória de **18 mm Hg** na pressão sistólica (**pulso paradoxal**) 5 dias após um IAM sugerem **ruptura de parede livre** com **tamponamento cardíaco**. O ecocardiograma mostra líquido pericárdico comprimindo as câmaras direitas, com **colapso diastólico do ventrículo direito**. O infarto de ventrículo direito é a alternativa tentadora porque também causa hipotensão, estase jugular e pulmões limpos, mas ocorre no IAM **inferior**, nas primeiras horas ou dias, e não causa bulhas abafadas nem pulso paradoxal acentuado. Um folheto mitral em *flail* e um jato através do septo produziriam, cada um, um novo sopro.
